program: Free medical, sexual-health, dental, counseling, benefits and outreach services

evidence.result: The Form 990 reports 2,007 clients and 3,153 encounters on $453,528 of annual expense. Current service disclosures indicate limited operations during transition, including paused dental and TB services.
evidence.transfer: These figures anchor costs and delivery scale, not causal health gains. No service-line outcome, treatment-linkage, or client-residence dataset was located. The model uses explicit priors rather than presenting encounters as QALYs.

evidence.population: High-risk women in an external chlamydia-screening trial
evidence.result: Among 2,607 randomized women, verified pelvic inflammatory disease occurred in 9 of 1,009 assigned screening and 33 of 1,598 assigned usual care; reported relative risk was 0.44 (95% CI 0.20–0.90). Only 64% of the screening arm was screened; 7% of those screened tested positive and were treated.
evidence.transfer: This supports a plausible testing-to-treatment mechanism, but it does not estimate Berkeley Free Clinic's effect. Its patient mix, positivity, alternative care and completed treatment are unknown; the trial effect is not multiplied by every clinic client.

evidence.population: Low-income adults in the Oregon Medicaid experiment
evidence.design: Randomized access to insurance, two-year follow-up
evidence.result: The study found greater healthcare use and detection, fewer positive depression screens and less financial strain, without significant improvement in measured physical-health outcomes over two years.
evidence.transfer: Coverage expansion is not the same intervention as a volunteer clinic. This mixed evidence argues against assuming that additional access reliably produces large health gains; it is contextual evidence, not a clinic-specific QALY conversion.

nutshell.headline: Very low cash cost and volunteer leverage create upside, but current limited operations, unknown service mix and unpriced marginal clinical throughput make health impact highly uncertain.
nutshell.body: Our signed whole-organization model estimates $3.85 million donated per 10 Bay-resident QALYs after an assumed residence allocation, compared with $3.62 million per 10 modeled QALYs across all beneficiaries. Verified complete gross resources are unavailable; an all-beneficiary volunteer-inclusive proxy is $12.28 million.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: The clinic reports 2,007 clients and 3,153 encounters on $453,528 expense and delivers free testing/treatment with 150 volunteers. A March 2026 City record links a $196,809 renovation to expanded capacity and hours.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Dental/TB are paused during a move, service-line outcomes are unpublished, public lab funding overlaps, and total net assets/fund balances have unreported restriction and availability.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Obtain the added clients/hours attributable to the renovated facility, a restored-service timeline, unduplicated service-line counts, positivity/treatment/linkage and current volunteer/resource requirements.

programSection.body: Berkeley Community Health Project, DBA Berkeley Free Clinic, is an independent volunteer-run clinic. FY2025 filing reports 2,007 clients, 3,153 encounters and $453,528 whole expense.

steps.title: Test and treat infections
steps.detail: Current STI testing/treatment plus HIV/hepatitis screening and referral; positivity/linkage not reported.

steps.title: Provide medical and dental access
steps.detail: FY2025 includes acute/preventive care; dental and TB are currently paused during transition.

steps.title: Offer counseling and navigation
steps.detail: Peer counseling, referrals and benefits enrollment receive no separate QALYs.

steps.title: Mobilize volunteers
steps.detail: 150 volunteers and seven employees are reported; current volunteer hours are unavailable.

programSection.boundary: All FY2025 expense is charged against reported clinical clients. Nonclinical activity and transition costs reflected in that filing receive zero separate benefit; the accounting relationship of the separately reported $196,809 renovation is unknown. A general gift is not modeled as STI-only.

model.headline: Prior-weighted $3.62M per 10 QALYs; central $4.78M.
model.body: A $100,000 gift is scaled against whole expense and the 2,007-client denominator, then separately discounted for funding additionality, current capacity, uniqueness and material health realization. Finite signed QALYs are applied only after those gates.

inputs.label: Whole expense/client unit
inputs.basis: Form 990; clients not explicitly labeled unduplicated.

inputs.label: Funding additionality
inputs.basis: Deficit and current renovation funding request versus public funding and substantial cash/investments of unreported restriction/availability.

inputs.label: Current-service transfer
inputs.basis: Limited operation; dental/TB paused during move; City says renovated facility will expand capacity/hours but does not quantify them.

inputs.label: Unique-client factor
inputs.basis: Filing says clients but does not publish deduplication method.

inputs.label: Clients with material health gain
inputs.basis: Unknown service mix, positivity, treatment and linkage.

inputs.label: QALY per health-benefiting client
inputs.basis: Explicit finite acute/morbidity priors: central0.04 utility gain for0.5year=.02 QALY; cautious0.02 for0.5year=.01; favorable0.06 for1year=.06; harm−0.004 for0.5year=−.002. These are illustrative utility-duration packages, not measured effects; no mortality extrapolation.

inputs.label: Volunteer-inclusive resource proxy
inputs.basis: Undated archival listing indexed at approximately 2013: 31,000 hours/180 volunteers, scaled to current 150 under an unchanged-hours-per-volunteer assumption and valued at $40.14/hour; not current measured gross.

inputs.label: Scenario weights
inputs.basis: Direct current outcomes and marginal capacity absent.

sensitivity.headline: $3.62M per 10
sensitivity.detail: 0.27644 QALY; 79.84% from favorable tail; volunteer proxy $12.28M.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Without the favorable case, donor cost is $17.05M per 10 QALYs. Every health input is a prior rather than a BFC-measured effect.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 deficit $81,552; total net assets/fund balances $1.193M with restriction/availability unreported; cash/investments $1.049M. The $196,809 renovation was already undertaken and is linked to capacity/hours, but added clinical throughput and its accounting relationship to FY2025 expense are unreported. City lab contract is up to $150,000 over three years; actual draw and marginal private gap remain unverified.

reservations: Current limited-service mix differs from FY2025 throughput.
No service-line count, positivity, treatment completion or achieved health outcomes were found.
The favorable 5% case supplies 79.84% of signed benefit.
Volunteer-inclusive resources use an undated, approximately 2013 archival hours proxy and are not verified complete gross.
The $196,809 renovation is not reconciled to FY2025 expense and has no added-throughput denominator.
Bay/SF residence is unmeasured; displayed local shares are priors.
Total net assets/fund balances have unreported restriction/availability; cash/investments and public lab support make marginal funding additionality uncertain.
excludedBenefits: Avoided transmission, deaths or lifetime tails not captured by finite blended prior
